title: Father playing the Santa Barbara hotel above Paul Whiteman
summary: His father played upstairs while Whiteman's band played in the cellar.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yes, yes, I know, (inaudible). Earlier you mentioned something about your father's band in Santa Barbara that I thought was kind of interesting.

Oh, yeah, I was just thinking about thing. He used to laugh and make jokes about it. My dad was a very jovial type of guy. He was a big man. He was 255 pounds, well over six feet and fast on his feet, great dancer and a whole lot of fun. He used to laugh about the time when he came down from San Francisco to work in the Santa Barbara Hotel in Santa Barbara, California, which I think that particular hotel was rather severely damaged in the severe earthquake that we had of 1934 or right before 1934, when they had the big Santa Barbara earthquake. I don't know whether they had to demolish it or not.

But he was called to play with his orchestra for a course of time in the main dining room of the Santa Barbara Hotel for the dinners and such, and lo and behold, the band that was playing down in the cellar was the great white father, Paul Whiteman.
The King of Jazz. He was working in the cellar and my old man was working in the main dining room.
Of course, he got a little bit big after that. But it just shows you how things can happen to people. If you've got it or who you are, you are.
Obviously (Inaudible) your father was a fine musician.
